title: A cortico-subthalamic circuit rapidly engages and releases inhibition of specific movements depending on the environmental context
experiments_summary: Fifteen Parkinson's Disease patients implanted with Medtronic Percept PC sensing-capable bilateral STN deep-brain stimulators performed a stimulus- and response-selective stopping task. The task consisted of 12 blocks (~684 trials total) with four trial types: bimanual Go trials (60%), unimanual Go trials (10%), signal trials with Global-Stop (10%), Selective-Stop (10%), and Ignore (10%) conditions. Stop-signal delays were adaptively staircase-adjusted to achieve ~50% stopping success. Simultaneous 64-channel scalp EEG (sampled at 5 kHz, Brain Products MRplus amplifiers), bilateral STN local field potentials (LFPs) wirelessly streamed from the Percept PC device at 250 Hz, and bilateral forearm EMG from the FDI muscles were recorded. EEG and LFP signals were precisely temporally aligned using a DBS on/off artifact procedure. Data were resampled to 500 Hz, bandpass filtered, and artifact-removed via visual inspection and ICA. EMG was converted to RMS power and z-scored. Stop-signal reaction time (SSRT) was estimated using the integration method with replacement of Go omissions. Multivariate EEG decoding was performed using a linear discriminant analysis-based decoder (ADAM toolbox) with leave-one-out cross-validation across six pairwise condition comparisons, tested for significance via cluster permutation statistics. Motor ICA components were identified and removed, and decoding was repeated on motor-artifact-free EEG to verify results. Full-spectrum event-related spectral perturbations (ERSPs) of EEG and LFP were computed via filter-Hilbert method (1–125 Hz) and tested with cluster-based permutation tests. Beta-frequency burst probability timelines were extracted using complex Morlet wavelet convolution (13–30 Hz, 18 frequencies) with burst detection defined as local maxima exceeding 2x median power (EEG) or 6x median power (LFP), then converted to continuous burst-rate timelines via Gaussian convolution. Cortico-subthalamic connectivity was assessed by identifying post-STN-burst beta activity across EEG channels, tested with one-tailed t-tests corrected for multiple comparisons. STN-to-STN connectivity was assessed by time-locking each STN's burst-rate timeline around bursts in the contralateral STN, tested with FDR-corrected sample-wise t-tests. STN-to-STN phase coherence was assessed using filter-Hilbert-derived phase-angle differences, tested with cluster-based permutation tests. SSRT-locked cortico-subthalamic beta-band connectivity was analyzed by correlating windowed (50 ms) channel-wise EEG beta power with STN beta power across pre- and post-SSRT windows, Fisher's z-transformed and tested with t-tests corrected for multiple comparisons. A time-lagged sample-to-sample ROI-based cortico-subthalamic connectivity analysis was performed by correlating trial-wise beta power time series between nine EEG scalp ROIs and each STN across a 2,000 ms SSRT-locked window, tested via cluster-based permutation statistics. DBS electrode locations were reconstructed using LeadDBS from pre-operative MRI and post-operative MRI or CT scans.
